facts.statement: The study identifies a common genetic variant in modern humans that was inherited from Neandertals and affects the size of the occipital brain region.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: This genetic variant is located near the DAAM1 gene, which plays a role in brain development, within regions where transcription factors are expected to bind.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: People carrying the Neandertal variant show changes in DAAM1 gene activity and have occipital lobes that are approximately 0.85 cubic centimeters smaller for each copy of the variant they possess.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Individuals with two copies of the Neandertal variant have a nearly 10% lower risk of schizophrenia, a pattern not seen when looking at Neandertal ancestry in general.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The link between the variant and education level is minimal, corresponding to no more than two weeks of schooling per variant copy compared to an average of 15 years.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The Neandertal-derived variant is connected to changes in brain structure and a lower risk of schizophrenia, but it has little to no relationship with general cognitive ability.
facts.subject: humans
